syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: Defining psychology: mental processes, experience and behaviour

concepts.learning_objective: Students will state the formal definition of psychology and the origin of the term.
Students will distinguish mental processes from brain activity and explain why experiences are subjective.
Students will classify behaviours as overt or covert and relate them to stimulus and response.

topics.title: Psychology as a discipline: natural science and social science
topics.ncert_sections: Psychology as a Discipline; Psychology as a Natural Science; Psychology as a Social Science

concepts.learning_objective: Students will explain how the hypothetico-deductive model guides psychology as a natural science.
Students will explain how psychology studies individuals in their socio-cultural context.
Students will explain why the mind is considered distinct from, though dependent on, the brain.
Students will describe evidence from affective neuroscience that the mind influences bodily processes.

topics.title: Popular notions about psychology
topics.ncert_sections: Popular Notions about the Discipline of Psychology

concepts.learning_objective: Students will explain why common-sense explanations of behaviour rely on hindsight.
Students will interpret Dweck's study as an example of scientific findings that run against common sense.
Students will compare Wundt's structuralism with James's functionalism.
Students will describe Gestalt psychology and behaviourism as reactions to structuralism.
Students will distinguish psychoanalytic, humanistic, cognitive and constructivist perspectives.
Students will identify the landmarks of the modern era of psychology in India.
Students will sequence Durganand Sinha's four phases of psychology in India.
Students will match problems to the appropriate branch of psychology.
Students will distinguish a clinical psychologist from a psychiatrist.

topics.title: Psychology, other disciplines and everyday life
topics.ncert_sections: Psychology and Other Disciplines; Psychology in Everyday Life

concepts.learning_objective: Students will explain how psychology contributes to and draws from other disciplines.
Students will apply psychological understanding to personal and social problems in daily life.
Identify description, prediction, explanation, control and application as the goals of psychological enquiry.
Distinguish between prediction, explanation and control of behaviour with examples.

topics.title: Steps in scientific research and alternative paradigms
topics.ncert_sections: Steps in Conducting Scientific Research; Alternative Paradigms of Research

concepts.learning_objective: Sequence the four steps of scientific research and explain the role of a hypothesis.
Contrast the scientific and interpretive traditions of psychological research.
Explain why psychological data are tied to context, method and theory.
Classify information as demographic, physical, physiological or psychological data.
Describe selection, recording and analysis in scientific observation and the risk of observer bias.
Distinguish naturalistic from controlled and participant from non-participant observation.

topics.title: Experimental method
topics.ncert_sections: Experimental Method; Box 2.1; Field Experiments and Quasi Experiments

concepts.learning_objective: Identify independent, dependent and extraneous variables in an experiment.
Explain experimental and control groups and techniques such as elimination, matching, counter-balancing and random assignment.
Distinguish laboratory, field and quasi experiments and evaluate their strengths and limits.
Interpret positive, negative and zero correlation coefficients ranging from +1.0 to -1.0.
Compare interviews, questionnaires and telephone surveys and state the strengths and limits of surveys.

topics.title: Psychological testing and case study
topics.ncert_sections: Psychological Testing; Types of Tests; Case Study

concepts.learning_objective: Explain objectivity, reliability, validity and norms of a standardised test.
Classify tests as verbal, non-verbal or performance, individual or group, and speed or power.
Describe the case study method, its uses and its limitations.

topics.title: Analysis of data, limitations and ethical issues
topics.ncert_sections: Analysis of Data; Limitations of Psychological Enquiry; Ethical Issues

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish quantitative from qualitative analysis of data.
Explain the lack of a true zero point, relative nature of tools and subjective interpretation as limitations.
Apply the ethical principles of voluntary participation, informed consent, debriefing, sharing results and confidentiality.

topics.title: Meaning of development and the life-span perspective
topics.ncert_sections: Meaning of Development; Life-Span Perspective; Box 3.1

concepts.learning_objective: Define development and distinguish it from growth, maturation and evolution.
Explain the assumptions of the life-span perspective on development.
Distinguish genotype from phenotype and explain how heredity sets limits on development.
Explain how genes and environment interact, including Scarr's view of parent-provided and child-chosen environments.
Identify the microsystem, mesosystem, exosystem, macrosystem and chronosystem in Bronfenbrenner's contextual view.
Describe Durganand Sinha's two-layer ecological model of child development in the Indian context.

topics.title: Developmental stages and the prenatal stage
topics.ncert_sections: Overview of Developmental Stages; Prenatal Stage

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what developmental stages and developmental tasks are.
Identify maternal factors and teratogens that affect prenatal development.
Describe newborn reflexes, motor skills and sensory abilities.
Explain sensorimotor thinking and object permanence in infancy.
Explain attachment, Harlow's contact-comfort study and Erikson's trust versus mistrust.

topics.title: Childhood
topics.ncert_sections: Childhood; Box 3.2 Gender and Sex Roles

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the cephalocaudal and proximodistal trends and motor skill development in childhood.
Distinguish preoperational features (egocentrism, animism, centration) from concrete operational thought.
Describe the development of self, gender roles and Kohlberg's moral reasoning in childhood.
Describe pubertal changes and formal operational thought in adolescence.
Explain imaginary audience, personal fable and identity formation in adolescence.
Identify features of delinquency, substance abuse and eating disorders in adolescence.
Describe the tasks, roles and physical and cognitive changes of adulthood.
Explain the challenges of old age such as retirement, widowhood and dependency.

topics.title: Knowing the world: stimuli, sense modalities and thresholds
topics.ncert_sections: Knowing the World; Nature and Varieties of Stimulus; Sense Modalities

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the seven sense organs, including the two deep senses, and define sensation and sense modality.
Explain the absolute threshold and why it is estimated over many trials.
Distinguish the difference threshold from the absolute threshold in a given situation.
Describe alertness, concentration and search as properties of attention, and its focus and fringe.
Classify external and internal factors that determine selective attention.
Compare the filter, filter-attenuation and multimode theories of selective attention.

topics.title: Sustained attention, span of attention, divided attention and ADHD

concepts.learning_objective: Explain vigilance and the factors that facilitate or inhibit sustained attention.
State the span of attention and explain when attention can be divided.
Describe the features, causes and management of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder.

topics.title: Perceptual processes and the perceiver
topics.ncert_sections: Perceptual Processes; Processing Approaches in Perception; The Perceiver

concepts.learning_objective: Define perception and distinguish bottom-up from top-down processing.
Explain how motivation, expectations and cultural experience shape perception.
Distinguish field dependent and field independent cognitive styles.
Explain the Gestalt view of form perception and the features of figure and ground.
Apply the Gestalt principles of organisation to visual patterns.

topics.title: Perception of space, depth and distance
topics.ncert_sections: Perception of Space, Depth, and Distance; Monocular Cues and Binocular Cues

concepts.learning_objective: Identify monocular (pictorial and kinetic) cues to depth in given scenes.
Explain retinal disparity, convergence and accommodation as cues to depth.
Distinguish size, shape and brightness constancy.
Explain geometrical and apparent movement illusions and why illusions occur.
Interpret cross-cultural findings on susceptibility to visual illusions.
Explain how cultural exposure to pictures affects pictorial perception.
Define learning as a relatively permanent change in behaviour or behavioural potential produced by experience.
Distinguish learning from temporary changes due to fatigue, habituation and drugs.
Explain that learning is an inferred process, different from observed performance.

topics.title: Classical Conditioning
topics.ncert_sections: Classical Conditioning; Determinants of Classical Conditioning

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the US, UR, CS and CR in Pavlov's experiment and everyday examples.
Compare simultaneous, delayed, trace and backward conditioning procedures.
Explain how appetitive or aversive US and the intensity of the CS affect conditioning.

topics.title: Operant/Instrumental Conditioning
topics.ncert_sections: Operant/Instrumental Conditioning; Determinants of Operant Conditioning; Box 5.1

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Skinner's operant conditioning and the nature of operants.
Distinguish positive reinforcement, negative reinforcement and punishment.
Explain how number, amount, quality, schedule and delay of reinforcement influence operant learning.
Distinguish primary and secondary reinforcers.
Explain extinction, resistance to extinction and spontaneous recovery.
Differentiate generalisation from discrimination and explain learned helplessness.
Explain observational learning using Bandura's Bobo doll study.
Describe Kohler's insight learning in chimpanzees.
Explain Tolman's latent learning and the idea of a cognitive map.
Describe paired-associates learning, serial learning and free recall.
Explain the determinants of verbal learning, including meaningfulness and the total time principle.
Explain category clustering and subjective organisation in free recall.

topics.title: Skill Learning and Factors Facilitating Learning

concepts.learning_objective: Identify Fitts' cognitive, associative and autonomous phases of skill acquisition.
Explain the partial reinforcement effect and the role of motivation in learning.
Explain preparedness for learning as a continuum set by biological constraints.
Describe the nature and origin of learning disabilities.
Identify the major symptoms of learning disabilities, including dyslexia.

topics.title: Nature of memory: encoding, storage and retrieval

concepts.learning_objective: Describe memory as the three interrelated stages of encoding, storage and retrieval.

topics.title: The stage model: sensory, short-term and long-term memory
topics.ncert_sections: Information Processing Approach: The Stage Model; Memory Systems

concepts.learning_objective: Compare the capacity, duration and encoding of sensory, short-term and long-term memory in the Atkinson-Shiffrin model.
Explain how attention, maintenance rehearsal, chunking and elaborative rehearsal move information between stores.

topics.title: Working memory and evaluation of the stage model

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the phonological loop, visuospatial sketchpad and central executive in Baddeley's working memory.
Evaluate evidence such as the case of KF that questions separate STM and LTM stores.
Explain Craik and Lockhart's structural, phonetic and semantic levels of processing and their effect on retention.

topics.title: Types of long-term memory
topics.ncert_sections: Types of Long-term Memory; Box 6.2; Box 6.3

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish declarative from procedural memory with examples.
Distinguish Tulving's episodic and semantic memory.
Describe flashbulb, autobiographical and implicit memory and methods such as recall, recognition and priming.

topics.title: Nature and causes of forgetting
topics.ncert_sections: Nature and Causes of Forgetting; Box 6.4

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret Ebbinghaus's curve of forgetting and evaluate trace decay theory.
Distinguish proactive from retroactive interference.
Explain forgetting due to absent or inappropriate retrieval cues.

topics.title: Enhancing memory
topics.ncert_sections: Enhancing Memory; Mnemonics using Images and Organisation

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the keyword method and the method of loci.
Apply chunking and the first letter technique to organise material.
Explain deep processing, minimising interference, retrieval cues and the PQRST method.

topics.title: Nature of Thinking and Building Blocks of Thought
topics.ncert_sections: Nature of Thinking; Building Blocks of Thought; Box 7.1

concepts.learning_objective: Describe thinking as a higher mental process that manipulates information and is inferred from behaviour.
Distinguish mental images and concepts as the building blocks of thought and explain why concepts are formed.
Explain how culture shapes analytical and holistic styles of thinking.

topics.title: Problem Solving and Its Obstacles
topics.ncert_sections: Problem Solving; Obstacles to Solving Problems

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the sequence of mental operations involved in solving a problem.
Explain how mental set and functional fixedness hinder problem solving.
Recognise lack of motivation and persistence as an obstacle to problem solving.
Distinguish deductive reasoning (general to particular) from inductive reasoning (particular to general).
Explain analogy as a four-part form of reasoning.
Explain how judgment and decision-making are interrelated yet different processes.
State the criteria of creative thinking: novelty, originality, effective surprise and appropriateness.
Distinguish convergent from divergent thinking and identify fluency, flexibility, originality and elaboration.
Explain de Bono's lateral thinking and the six thinking hats technique.

topics.title: Process and Strategies of Creative Thinking
topics.ncert_sections: Process of Creative Thinking; Strategies for Creative Thinking

concepts.learning_objective: Sequence the stages of preparation, incubation, illumination and verification.
Explain the principle of brainstorming and other strategies that enhance creative thinking.
Explain Whorf's linguistic relativity hypothesis and its strong version.
Compare Piaget's and Vygotsky's views on the relationship between thought and language.

topics.title: Development of Language and Language Use
topics.ncert_sections: Development of Language and Language Use; Box 7.3

concepts.learning_objective: Identify symbols, rules and communication as the basic characteristics of language.
Sequence the stages of language development from crying to telegraphic speech.
Compare Skinner's learning view and Chomsky's innate view of language acquisition, and explain pragmatic language use.

topics.title: Nature of motivation and the motivational cycle
topics.ncert_sections: Nature of Motivation; The Motivational Cycle

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the meaning of motivation and how motives help explain and predict behaviour.
Describe the sequence of need, drive, goal-directed behaviour and drive reduction in the motivational cycle.

topics.title: Types of motives and biological motives
topics.ncert_sections: Types of Motives; Biological Motives (Hunger, Thirst, Sex)

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish biological and psychosocial motives and explain their interdependence.
Define instinct as an inborn, biologically determined pattern of behaviour.
Explain the internal and external bases of hunger, thirst and the sex drive.
Describe the need for affiliation and McClelland's four ways of expressing the power motive.
Explain the features and sources of the need for achievement (n-Ach).
Explain curiosity and exploration as motives without a specific identifiable goal.
Arrange the five levels of Maslow's hierarchy in order and identify a need at each level.
Describe the characteristics of a self-actualised person and the limits of the hierarchy.
Distinguish emotion from feeling and mood.
Compare the six universally recognised emotions with the basic emotions proposed by Izard and Plutchik.
Explain how intensity, quality, gender and situation influence emotional experience.

topics.title: Expression of emotions and culture
topics.ncert_sections: Expression of Emotions; Culture and Emotional Expression; Culture and Emotional Labeling

concepts.learning_objective: Identify verbal and non-verbal channels of emotional expression, including paralanguage.
Explain cultural differences in gaze behaviour and emotional labeling.

topics.title: Managing negative emotions and enhancing positive emotions
topics.ncert_sections: Managing Negative Emotions; Box 8.1; Box 8.2; Managing your Anger; Enhancing Positive Emotions

concepts.learning_objective: Apply strategies such as self-monitoring, self-modeling and cognitive restructuring to manage emotions.
Distinguish monitoring and blunting strategies for examination anxiety and describe PTSD.
Explain the bases of anger management and the functions and enhancement of positive emotions.
